children: (BPCL) is set to tap the local corporate debt market after a gap of almost four years, looking to fund large planned capital expenditure, two merchant bankers directly aware of the matter said on Tuesday.

BPCL has plans to raise around 90 billion rupees ($961.08 million) through the sale of debt, but could approach the market in tranches, with the quantum on the said issue still under discussion, the bankers said, declining to be identified as they are not authorised to speak to the media.
"BPCL has started the preliminary discussions with bankers and is hinting at a tenor of around five years and should get done with the issue before end of December," one of the bankers said.
The state-run oil marketing company did not respond to a Reuters email seeking comment.

The bonds are rated AAA by Crisil, which said the company's rating reflects its strong market position in the domestic oil refining and marketing sector, and its strategic importance to the central government.

The company has sizeable capex plans of around 250 billion rupees to 300 billion rupees annually over fiscals 2027, 2028 and 2029, primarily towards refinery expansion and petrochemical projects, Crisil said in its rating note dated October 26.
"The proceeds should be utilised for capex, as refinancing needs are minimum," the second banker said.
The company does not have any outstanding bonds, after its five-year debt security matured at the end of October.
It had last tapped the rupee bond market in March 2023, when it raised 9.35 billion rupees through three-year bonds at an annual coupon of 7.58%.
